newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Mediolanum 1997 H1 fund inflows up. [corrected 19:02 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Italy's Mediolanum 1997 H1 fund inflows up. [corrected 19:02 gmt]

text.p: Italian insurance and financial services group Mediolanum SpA said its gross investment fund inflows rose 50 percent in the first half 1997 while life insurance premium income rose 35 percent.
The company is jointly owned by Silvio Berlusconi's Fininvest SpA and Mediolanum managing director Ennio Doris.

The company said in a statement that total life insurance premium income was 699 billion lire, but said that even if the positive trend continued in the second half it saw the growth rate slowing from the 35 percent increase seen in the first six months.
Its Mediolanum Gestione Fondi fund management arm posted total gross inflows of 1.469 (corrects from 1.237) trillion lire against 977 billion in the first half of 1996.

It added in the statement that following the Bank of Italy's approval, its securities broking subsidiary Programma Italia Investimenti Sim will become a bank with the name of Banca Mediolanum and start operating later this year.
